# glinet_fan (Resource)

Sets the temperature at which the fan of the router starts (`fan.get_config` and `fan.set_config`). The router has one fan configuration, so use one instance of this resource. Only a router with a fan (`hardware_feature.fan` of `system.get_info`) has this setting: on other routers, create and update fail and do not write to the router. For the speed of the fan, use the data source `glinet_fan_status`. The write was tested on a GL-AXT1800 with firmware 4.8.3: the router accepted `temperature` 60, and the fan started. Destroy removes the resource from the Terraform state and does not change the router.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The fan starts when the CPU temperature is more than 75 °C.
resource "glinet_fan" "this" {
  temperature = 75
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `temperature` (Number) The fan starts when the CPU temperature is more than this value, in °C (`temperature` in the router API). The web UI lets you select 70 to 90. The provider accepts 0 to 90: a value more than 90 can let the router get too hot before the fan starts, and a lower value only makes the fan run more. A GL-AXT1800 on firmware 4.8.3 accepted 60, and the fan started. Other values less than 70 were not tested on a router.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Always `fan`.
- `warn_temperature` (Number) Temperature in °C that the router gives and that you cannot set (`warn_temperature` in the router API). The web UI shows a warning when `temperature` is this value or less. If a write changes it is not known.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The import ID is always "fan".
terraform import glinet_fan.this fan
```
